findings.vulnerability_type_claimed: Unprotected initializer allows ownership takeover (proxy/upgrade admin hijack)
findings.reason: The finding identifies a real vulnerability in the `initializeTokenomics` function. The root cause is the lack of access control on the initialization function, allowing any caller to set themselves as the owner and configure critical system addresses. The location matches the vulnerable code. The attack scenario is concrete: an attacker can front-run the initialization to gain ownership and then upgrade the implementation or change manager addresses to hijack the protocol. The impact is a complete takeover of the system. This is a different vulnerability than the ground truth (which concerns checkpoint timing manipulation), so it qualifies as BONUS_VALID.

notes: The model found a valid vulnerability (unprotected initializer) but did not identify the target vulnerability (checkpoint timing manipulation). The target vulnerability requires identifying that services can manipulate checkpoint timing to benefit from reward droughts in the `checkpoint` function, which the model did not report.
